What you can do with dsOMOP

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-showcase.Rmd
book-showcase.Rmd

What you will learn

See six useful results, then choose the chapter that teaches your next step.

Read the cards as a tour, or run them in order after the Opal login in Getting started. The first four cards use the 48-person synthetic questionnaire study on two sites; the last two use Synthea27Nj labs.

library(dsOMOPClient)
conns <- ds.omop.login(rep("https://localhost:8443", 2), user = "administrator",
  password = "password",
  server = c("site", "site2"),
  resource = c(site = "omop.questionnaire", site2 = "omop.questionnaire_site2"))$conns

Named concepts across sites

The education question is 900001, found in chapter 4’s catalogue. The recipe takes each person’s latest answer. By default, the same concept ID gets the same name across sites, using the newest available vocabulary wording.

education <- omop_variable(event = omop_event("observation", 900001L),
  reducer = omop_reduce("last_value", value = "value_as_concept_id"))
named <- omop_recipe(variables = list(education = education))
recipe_execute(named, out = c(output = "D_tour_named"), conns = conns)
education_counts <- dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_tour_named$education",
  useNA = "always", datasources = conns)
education_counts$output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_counts
site site2
Secondary education 12 0
University qualification 12 24
NA 24 24

Site 1 has 12 Secondary and 12 University answers; site 2 has 0 and 24. Both use “University qualification”, the newer name for concept 900102. Each site also has 24 missing answers. A shared label does not imply equal counts. These two teaching sites are related copies for comparison, not independent study samples. Learn concepts and harmonisation →

The next three cards use one questionnaire site:

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(conns)
conns <- ds.omop.login("https://localhost:8443", user = "administrator",
  password = "password", resource = "omop.questionnaire", server = "site")$conns

Dates and completed ages

Completed age at death counts birthdays reached, using the available birth and death dates. Incomplete dates stay missing by default.

dates <- omop_recipe(variables = list(age = omop_age_at("death")))
recipe_execute(dates, out = c(output = "D_tour_dates"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.quantileMean("D_tour_dates$age", datasources = conns)
#>    5%   10%   25%   50%   75%   90%   95%  Mean
#> 32.00 32.00 32.75 37.50 42.25 43.00 43.00 37.50

The 24 complete ages are 32, 33, 42 and 43, with mean and median 37.5 years. The median is the midpoint of the middle two ages, 33 and 42; it is not an observed age. The other 24 people lack a complete birth date or a death record. Missing age at death is not an age of zero. Dates can also be grouped by month, quarter or year. Learn dates and ages →

Choose the output shape

A wide table has one row per participant; long retains visits; a panel repeats time bins; survival records follow-up until an outcome or censoring. Visit settings 9201 (inpatient) and 9202 (outpatient) come from chapter 4.

visits <- omop_event("visit_occurrence", c(9201L, 9202L), name = "visits")
visitors <- omop_population("visitors", index = omop_index(visits))
shapes <- list(
  omop_output("wide", rows = "visitors", format = "wide"),
  omop_output("long", rows = "visitors", format = "long", sources = "visits"),
  omop_output("panel", rows = "visitors", format = "person_period",
    options = list(sources = list(visits), bins = list(width = 30L),
      window = omop_window(1, 90), analyses = "count")),
  omop_output("survival", rows = "visitors", format = "survival",
    options = list(outcomes = list(revisit = visits), tar = omop_window(1, 365),
      censor = list("observation_end", "death"))))
study <- omop_recipe(events = list(visits), populations = list(visitors),
  variables = list(n_visits = omop_variable(event = visits, reducer = omop_reduce("count"))),
  outputs = shapes)
targets <- c(wide = "D_tour_wide", long = "D_tour_long",
  panel = "D_tour_panel", survival = "D_tour_survival")
recipe_execute(study, out = targets, conns = conns)
shape_sizes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(targets), function(shape)
  data.frame(Shape = shape, Rows = dsBaseClient::ds.dim(targets[[shape]],
    datasources = conns)[[1L]][1L])))
shape_sizes
Shape Rows
wide 36
long 60
panel 108
survival 36

All four use the same 36 visitors. Long has 60 visits; the panel has 108 rows (36 people × three 30-day bins). Wide and survival each have 36 rows. Repeated rows are not independent participants. Learn output formats →

A cause-of-death wide table

Give every person one row with their coded cause of death, then count the causes. The capstone adds age, education, fever and visit periods to the same table; the cause concepts come from chapter 4.

cause <- omop_variable(event = omop_event("death"),
  reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", value = "cause_concept_id"))
causes <- omop_recipe(variables = list(cause = cause),
  outputs = omop_output("people", format = "wide", grain = "person"))
recipe_execute(causes, out = c(people = "D_tour_causes"), conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_tour_causes$cause",
  useNA = "always", datasources = conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_tour_causes$cause
#> Myocardial infarction             Pneumonia                    NA
#>                    24                    12                    12

There are 24 myocardial infarction deaths, 12 pneumonia deaths and 12 people without a death record. The person key and individual answers stay private. Build and analyse this table →

Switch to Synthea27Nj for numeric values:

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
ds.omop.connect(resource = "omop.synthea", conns = conns)

Numbers and their groupings

Take each person’s mean haemoglobin, then compare means within three teaching bands. Measurement 3000963 and g/dL unit 8713 are identified in chapter 4.

hb <- omop_variable(event = omop_event("measurement", 3000963L,
  unit = omop_unit(8713L)), reducer = omop_reduce("mean"))
band_names <- c("below 14", "14 to below 15", "15 or above")
labs <- omop_recipe(variables = list(hb = hb,
  band = omop_number_bins(hb, breaks = c(-Inf, 14, 15, Inf), labels = band_names)))
recipe_execute(labs, out = c(output = "D_tour_labs"), conns = conns)
groups <- dsBaseClient::ds.meanSdGp("D_tour_labs$hb", "D_tour_labs$band",
  type = "combine", datasources = conns)
data.frame(`Band (g/dL)` = band_names,
  People = as.numeric(groups$Nvalid_gp), `Mean (g/dL)` = as.numeric(groups$Mean_gp),
  check.names = FALSE)
Band (g/dL) People Mean (g/dL)
below 14 9 13.34
14 to below 15 9 14.32
15 or above 10 15.61

The groups contain 9, 9 and 10 people, with means 13.34, 14.32 and 15.61 g/dL respectively. These are actual within-band means of person-level means. The breaks are teaching choices, not clinical reference ranges. Learn lab values, units and groupings →

Derive and filter without downloading rows

Convert the person means to g/L, then keep people at or above the teaching cutoff of 14 g/dL. Find the target unit by its exact name:

target_units <- ds.omop.concept.search("gram per liter", domain = "Unit",
  standard_only = FALSE, conns = conns)$pooled
target_unit <- target_units[target_units$concept_name == "gram per liter", ]
target_unit[c("concept_id", "concept_name")]
concept_id concept_name
8636 gram per liter 
gl_id <- target_unit$concept_id

The selected unit is 8636, gram per liter. One g/dL is ten g/L; the conversion changes the scale, while the filter below changes which people are included.

converted <- omop_recipe(variables = list(hb = hb,
  hb_gl = omop_number(hb, omop_number_spec(
    unit = omop_number_unit("unit:8713", paste0("unit:", gl_id), 10)))))
recipe_execute(converted, out = c(output = "D_tour_converted"), conns = conns)
ds.omop.mutate("D_tour_converted", above_cutoff = ifelse(hb >= 14, 1L, 0L),
  newobj = "D_tour_flagged", conns = conns)
ds.omop.filter("D_tour_flagged", expr = omop_where(above_cutoff == 1L),
  newobj = "D_tour_selected", conns = conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.mean("D_tour_selected$hb_gl", datasources = conns)$Mean.by.Study
EstimatedMean Nmissing Nvalid Ntotal
150 0 19 19

The selected group has 19 people with no missing haemoglobin means. Its mean is 150.00 g/L (15.00 g/dL), higher than the all-person mean of 144.67 g/L because the nine people below 14 g/dL were excluded. This is a teaching rule, not a diagnosis. Learn derived columns and filters →

Recap

Choose meanings, time, units and table shape; compute at the server and interpret the released summaries. Each linked chapter develops one of these decisions.
